prompts.name: Harsh Choices — anchored sidebar
prompts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: polished, production-quality concept screenshot for Legend of the Five Rings EMPEROR EDITION original collectible card game, running in Godot, 1920x1080 widescreen composition. This is a native game interface, not a website.
References: Image 1 is the existing in-game screenshot: preserve the actual navy-and-gold physical playmat, war-room backdrop, six-phase rail, two left clan placards, bottom full-card hand and physical card piles/rows; it establishes the exact layout. Image 2 is the APPROVED worn black lacquer UI design system: use this for beautiful tactile frame/button detail, aged brass edges and rivets, subtly scratched BLACK lacquer, cream typography. Image 3 is the original Event card; preserve this card's authentic illustration and card face in the source preview. Never invent a different card frame or anime illustration.
Typography: WeatheredQuill uppercase for major headings only, tightly spaced but not overlapping; elegant Caudex regular for readable body, bold for action labels, italic only for short quiet notes. Generous line height. No modern sans-serif dashboard styling, no olive-green rectangles, no excessive filigree inside reading areas.
Keep the board visible for context, mute unrelated actions while a decision is pending. No loading screens, arbitrary countdowns, generic OK/Continue confirmation, money/currency awards, or invented game mechanics. No close X/escape route that silently answers a pending choice. Match the phase and whose decision it is. Concept label must appear clearly but unobtrusively in the TOP LEFT of the outer image as a small editorial badge, distinct from game controls.
Render exact supplied UI text with immaculate spelling, legible and high contrast. Original fine print on reference cards may remain photographic. Avoid tiny lengthy explanations. Rich native game polish, restrained lighting, thin worn-metal hierarchy, consistent reusable components.
Concept label: "A1 · HARSH CHOICES · SIDEBAR".
Scenario: local Crane player's Events phase, four surviving provinces. Harsh Choices is revealed in their Province 2. Highlight EVENTS on the phase bar and the Crane placard's "YOUR DECISION"; suppress the old "You may act or pass". No active red battlefield, no attack buttons.
Composition: original right sidebar approximately 27% wide. The new decision fills that existing sidebar. Preserve the table composition; gently brighten only local Province 2 with a fine gold outline, a small numeral 2 below it, and the authentic Harsh Choices card sitting in it. No other province selectable.
Right panel hierarchy, top to bottom:
small context "EVENT · YOUR CHOICE"
large heading "HARSH CHOICES"
short location "Your Province 2"
centered authentic full Event-card preview, about 170x240px, enough breathing room.
body "Destroy this province to draw 3 cards?"
a restrained consequence row with a broken-gate icon and three cards icon:
"Provinces 4 → 3" and "Draw 3 cards".
two generous full-width options, both readable and unambiguous, no extra confirm:
neutral black lacquer button "Keep province"
deep muted vermilion lacquer button with brass edge "Destroy province · Draw 3".
Below these a quiet short note "The province is permanently lost." Keep loss information near the destructive button. No red rectangle around an already destroyed province, no positive green checkmarks or default selected action.
Finish with no persistent battle log under these decisions. Board remains sufficiently visible to evaluate which province is at stake. Show optional decision as optional, never claim drawing is compulsory.

Scenario: battle decision interrupted by opponent's Times of Strife; local Crane player must discard exactly one card from their hand. Show ATTACK active on the phase bar and local Crane's "YOUR DECISION". Remove misleading "You may act or pass", battle Pass button, and unrelated choices. No pending card identity is visible to the opponent.
Composition: right sidebar approximately 27% wide, same tactile frame, spacing and typographic hierarchy as an approved game menu. Full hand at bottom stays in its original place and has clearly separated full card faces. Show the actual visible hand card "Never Afraid" slightly raised with thin ivory-gold edge and small checkmark, the rest remain selectable and unraised; ONE selected card only.
Right panel, top to bottom:
small context "BATTLE · DISCARD REQUIRED"
large heading "TIMES OF STRIFE"
small authentic full Event card preview beside a concise source caption "Opponent's Event".
body, wrapped with breathing room: "You announced a Battle action with no units at this battlefield."
larger instruction "Choose 1 card from your hand."
selection row "Selected: Never Afraid" and quiet "1 of 1".
a full-width aged gold button "Discard Never Afraid"
small understated text action "Clear selection".
Do not add a full extra duplicate gallery of hand cards in the sidebar. Indicate the selected card goes to the Fate discard pile through a tiny clear destination label "To Fate discard" near the selected row, not a huge line across the board. Keep selected card name readable, not italic.
This is the ready-to-discard state; no button to skip the obligation, no Cancel or Pass that would bypass it. A click selects only, the explicit discard button commits. After submission play resumes automatically; do NOT render another Continue button.

Composition: alternative to the tall sidebar decision. Retain a narrow, quiet ordinary right rail but make the actual choice a beautifully proportioned landscape lacquer panel floating in the center-right of the playable area, above the local province row without covering that row or the hand. About 900px wide and 420px tall at 1920x1080. Preserve visible province 2 below it, highlighted thin gold with a tiny pointer connecting the panel to that one province. Rest of board slightly dimmed, NOT blacked out.
Panel has ornate but refined aged-brass frame corners, real-looking black lacquer grain, source-card preview in a narrow left third, choices in right two thirds. Header is "HARSH CHOICES", context "Your Province 2 · Optional".
Show the full authentic Event card at left. At right a clear question "Keep your province, or draw 3 cards?"
Under this, two equally sized tactile option tiles side by side:
Left tile: simple gold intact-gate icon, "Keep province", quiet "4 provinces remain".

Each tile is itself an actionable option, no separate Select/Confirm/Continue. Use neutral black lacquer on keep and very deep wine lacquer on destroy, no green recommendations. Small quiet line below choices "Destroying the province is permanent."
Do not show an image of a province already burning: this is still a decision. No extra confirmation dialog, no dismiss X. Explicit benefits and cost in the action tiles allow a deliberate choice. This panel should feel like a refined game interaction in the existing room, not an infographic or a collection of wireframes.
